summary.intent: Get PR #105 (span hit ownership, with #107 merged in) unblocked and mergeable by resolving its conflict with main and a review finding, then decide and start the next piece of work.
summary.outcome: A subagent merged main into #105, fixed the lossy-offset rescan finding with a linear one-pass implementation, and pushed 539e80ce, which is mergeable and waiting on CI and approval. A deterministic, model-free agent-workflow context-cost harness was started, and its decision-log notes went into docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md.

repo: The stacked span PRs conflicted because #106 and #108 merged into main after #107 had been merged into #105's branch; merging origin/main and the feat/span-hit-ownership branch resolved it with no rebase or force-push.
Decision-log sections are numbered, so merge conflicts there are resolved by renumbering (this PR's section became §43, #107's became §44).
tests/scaling.rs was deleted on main by #106, so it was removed during the merge.
#108's name boost shifted ranking scores, so three expected strings in cli.rs (scores and one snippet) had to be updated to the combined state.
Verification commands are `just lint`, `just test`, `just changesets` and `just rg-compare`; rg-compare scores must stay at or above the baseline.
Merging #105 lands both span PRs, which are ADR 0005 PRs 2 and 3.

Per-line offset-to-lossy-text mapping should be a single forward pass over UTF-8 chunks, and the other per-match rescans (hit_line_starts, owned_hits sweep, find_matches, union_of_runs) each already make one pass.

code.finding: `lossy_offsets` / `lossy_runs` map a line's sorted offsets to lossy text in one forward pass over UTF-8 chunks. A counted-visits test shows len/2+1 visits at 1x, 2x and 4x line length, within len + ranges, with no wall-clock. The old per-offset function is kept in the tests as the oracle for a proptest on random invalid-UTF-8 lines.

workflow: Use counted-visit tests instead of wall-clock timing to assert linear complexity, since they are deterministic.
Keep the old implementation as a test oracle for property tests when replacing it with an optimized one.
Verify subagent reports against GitHub directly (mergeable state, finding list, CI status) rather than trusting them.
A report-only deterministic measure (bytes, estimated tokens as ceil(bytes/3), turns) can serve as a ratchet before paying for model-based evals.
Sequence work that touches the same code (the search sink) after the blocking PR merges.

friction: The subagent resolved the review finding just before its push landed, out of the order requested, so the finding briefly read as resolved while the fix was unpushed.
PR #105 conflicted with main because of the merge order of the stacked PRs #106, #107 and #108.
#105 is BLOCKED on pending CI and approval, so follow-up work that touches the search sink has to wait.
open_items: Merge PR #105 once CI finishes, and release PR #97, which is mergeable and waiting on the user.
Perf pass on the double `open` per file, the single-threaded directory walk (about 6%), and sizing the shared rayon pool per search.
Docs refresh so README, ARCHITECTURE and the architecture docs match the span, name and snippet changes.
Re-measure on final main, on a quiet machine, to settle the stress/many numbers.
Clean up the leftover agent worktrees and branches.
Make the context-cost harness gating: it currently only reports, with a failing marker if monokl's median bytes exceed rg's or the one-turn answerable rate falls below 0.8.
Possible later Haiku-versus-Sonnet model evals, after the deterministic ratchet exists.
